problem: The trap says {aⁿbⁿ} is generated both by S → aSb | ε and by S → ab | aSb. The second grammar can never produce ε, so it generates only {aⁿbⁿ : n ≥ 1}. This directly contradicts the answer to Q5, which correctly says G2 gives n ≥ 1 and cannot produce ε. A student revising from the trap will write the wrong language in the exam.
fix: Say: {aⁿbⁿ : n ≥ 1} is generated by S → ab | aSb as well as by S → aSb | ε with the ε case unused; to get all of {aⁿbⁿ : n ≥ 0} from a different rule list, use S → A, A → aAb | ε.

problem: It says the single rule S → aSb keeps the two counts equal. That rule alone never produces a terminal string; the base case S → ε is what ends the derivation.
fix: Say: the pair of rules S → aSb | ε adds one a at the front and one b at the back per step, and S → ε ends with the counts equal.

problem: Section 2 has just defined round brackets as a grouping shorthand on right sides. The very next bullet uses ( and ) as terminals in S → (S)S | ε, so a reader can mistake them for the grouping shorthand.
fix: Add one sentence: here ( and ) are terminals of the language, not the grouping shorthand; write them in bold or quotes once to make the difference clear.

problem: The first output line is the repr of the empty string, printed as '' on the same line as the label, so it reads as 'output: empty'. On a phone the four printed lines also lose their indentation.
fix: Put the output on separate labelled lines and add a note that the first line '' is the empty string printed with quotes: line for k = 0 is the empty string.

problem: 'They differ by ε only, so they are different grammars' draws the wrong conclusion. Two grammars with different rule lists can generate the same language; what matters is that the two languages differ.
fix: End with: L(G1) ≠ L(G2) because ε ∈ L(G1) but ε ∉ L(G2), so the two grammars are not equivalent.

problem: 'the same 4-tuple is what yacc, bison and ANTLR read as input' is loose. These tools read a grammar specification file (BNF or EBNF plus declarations and actions), not the 4-tuple itself.
fix: Say: the grammar these tools read is the same object, written in BNF or EBNF with declarations and actions added.

problem: 'marks leak away quietly there' is unclear for a reader with English as a second language.
fix: Say: writing aS → ab or SA → aA is not allowed, and examiners deduct marks for it without comment.

problem: The definition does not say that V and T are nonempty, which standard textbooks require together with finiteness and disjointness.
fix: Say: V and T are finite, nonempty, disjoint sets, and S ∈ V.
